definition: A 1.5B instruction-tuned Qwen, used across 4 sources as the small model where an intervention can be run cheaply and where a null is most likely to be about the model. Its appearances: as one of the 18 checkpoints in a cross-model cultural-knowledge audit, as the real pretrained model on which a closed-form cross-layer ablation bound is tested, as one of two small models in an interpretable adaptive-sampling controller whose maximum budget of eight and 256-token cap the authors flag as bounding what allocation can matter, and as a training backbone in medical reasoning.

evidence.note: Builds a parallel entity grid of 27 folk-narrative motifs across 10 cultures and instruments 18 models with probing, logit lens, activation patching and generation, finding that the residual stream separates cultures cleanly in every model while the readout collapses onto Greco-Roman defaults — so the failure is at the decoder, not the encoder.
evidence.title: Cultural Awareness is Represented but Not Decoded: Tracing Mythological Knowledge across 18 Open-Source LLMs

evidence.note: Extends a single-block interaction theorem to ablated subsets spanning many layers, isolates the cross-layer remainder as an exact double integral rather than bounding it, supplies the one missing closed-form ingredient (a local attention Jacobian bound, verified without a violation on a real 1.5B model), and tests the whole picture on an emergent circuit nobody designed for it — reporting the mixed outcome as mixed.
evidence.title: Cross-Layer Interaction under Weight-Space Ablation: A Closed-Form Attention Jacobian Bound and a Test on a Real Pretrained Model

evidence.note: Allocates test-time samples per prompt with a fuzzy controller over human-readable difficulty and confidence signals, and — under a selector-matched protocol that isolates the budget policy from the answer selector — reports the result honestly as an accuracy-compute tradeoff rather than an accuracy gain.
evidence.title: Interpretable Adaptive Sampling for LLM Test-Time Scaling

evidence.note: Replaces the single tolerance threshold that RLVR uses to score floating-point answers with a hybrid reward pairing a hard clinical-safety constraint against a continuous precision-sensitive term, and adds a reward for stating the computational formula explicitly so an external verifier can check it.
evidence.title: MedCalc-R1: Knowledge-Guided Reward Framework for Medical Mathematical Reasoning

name: Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct
